beginner.headline: Tomorrow (Sun Oct 18): conditional for beginners. Best 6:45–10:00 AM on the rising tide toward the 10:31 AM high (1.8 ft). East trades around 20 mph are forecast all day (zone forecast E 10–25 mph), a bit stronger than today, so drift is the main limit. 10:00 AM–12:30 PM conditional; from 12:30 PM not recommended. Evening forecast, lower confidence than a same-morning report; the morning on-site check decides.
beginner.recommendation: Plan an early start and keep it flexible. NWS has east winds around 20 mph for Oʻahu on Sunday (surf zone forecast) and E 10–25 mph for Honolulu Metro, with trades strengthening modestly tonight and Sunday; there is no sign in the forecasts of the light dawn wind this morning had, so expect drift from the start and check it at the beach. The south swell is easing: NWS says the ~15 s south-southwest swell keeps above-average south shore surf tonight and declines Sunday (surf zone forecast: south-facing 3–5 ft AM, 2–4 ft PM, exposed shores). The surf-forecast.com Waikīkī model has about 1.6 ft at 13 s Sunday morning, 1.3 ft by afternoon. Small at Canoes, but still long-period, so watch several full set cycles (10+ minutes) before committing. Water: DOH list not reachable; North Shore brown-water and bacteria advisories reported in news (Waimea Bay, Laniakea), nothing verified for Waikīkī either way. Showers are forecast in bursts tonight and Sunday night, mostly windward, so check water color at Canoes and toward the Kūhiō drains and Ala Wai side. One student or a small group of strong adults; several students or children only if drift is low at the start. Your on-site read overrides this report.

water.runoff: Brown, gray, cloudy or turbid water, or visible runoff: don't go in, advisory or not. DOH guidance: storm runoff can carry sewage and pathogens; stay out of affected water for 48–72 hours after rain stops.
